title: Commitment metric definitions and proportional degraded-capacity compensation proposal
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: define measurable commitment metrics for Dedicated capacity throughput guarantees, derive a proportional degraded-capacity compensation model (error-budget credits), and specify contract language that maps operational SLOs to customer remediation. This ticket collects engineering measurement proposals, legal-friendly contract snippets, and an operational playbook for issuing credits when service capacity is materially degraded. The output will be a single spec that PM, Legal, SRE, and Sales can use for new Dedicated contracts.
proposal_summary: We propose defining two primary commitment metrics: 'Serve Availability' (percentage of request tokens served within a committed latency band at a committed throughput), and 'Provisioned Throughput Compliance' (percentage of time the customer's reserved throughput is available at a specified queue depth). Credits are computed proportional to the measured shortfall: credit = committed_monthly_fee * (time_weighted_shortfall / billing_window). Shortfall uses a rolling 7-day measurement for operational alerts and a monthly aggregated measurement for billing credits. Autoscale and burst behaviors are explicitly carved out with deterministic rules (burst windows, queued requests, and pre-emption priorities).
measurement_spec: Primary signals: p50/p95/p99 request latency for generation requests, tokens_per_second served, and sustained accepted concurrent streams.
Measurement windows: realtime (1m/5m) for autoscale triggers, 7-day rolling window for outage classification, and calendar-month for crediting/charging calculations.
Granularity: 1-minute aggregated telemetry per customer/route; retention of raw summary for 90 days for dispute resolution.

Failure classification: an incident counts toward a shortfall only when Serve Availability < committed threshold for at least 15 continuous minutes and a customer-level queue begins dropping or timing out.
Edge cases: maintenance windows declared 72+ hours in advance are excluded; emergency mitigations with <1 hour notice are included but flagged in reports.
error_budget_formula: Let C = committed_throughput (tokens/sec), A_target = target Serve Availability (e.g., 99.9%), T_billing = seconds in billing window. For each second t, measure A_t = 1 if observed throughput >= C * allowed_variance and latency < latency_threshold else 0. time_weighted_shortfall = sum_over_t(max(0, A_target - A_t))/T_billing. credit = monthly_fee * time_weighted_shortfall. Example: committed 100k tokens/sec, A_target=0.999, measured shortfall accounts to 0.002 over month => credit = monthly_fee * 0.002. This formula supports proportional credits rather than binary SLA breach thresholds.
contract_snippet: Service Commitment: Redwood Inference will make available the committed throughput for Customer's Dedicated Capacity pool measured as 'Serve Availability' (defined in the Measurement Schedule).

Remediation: If the monthly Serve Availability falls below the committed threshold, Customer is eligible for a proportional service credit calculated using the time-weighted shortfall formula (Error Budget Formula).

Exclusions: Credits will not be issued for Excluded Events (scheduled maintenance, customer misconfiguration, force majeure). Burst behavior and preemption policies are described in Appendix A and do not count as breaches when operating within those defined behaviors.
Notice and Dispute: Customer must notify Redwood within 30 days of invoice issuance to request credit; Redwood will supply telemetry exports for the contested billing window.
remediation_playbook_steps: 1) Detection: Automated monitors flag Serve Availability < threshold for 15 continuous minutes and open PM ticket with severity and preliminary measurements.
2) Triage: SRE validates telemetry, checks autoscale events, and records if a denylist (maintenance/known incident) applies.

3) Mitigation: If capacity is constrained, trigger dedicated autoscale actions (grow pool if autoscale policy permits) and enable temporary spill-to-hosted model variants according to customer's config.
4) Postmortem: Run RCA, quantify time_weighted_shortfall for the billing window, draft credit calculation, and produce customer-facing incident summary within 7 business days.
5) Credit issuance: Finance issues proportional credit on the next invoice cycle; if contested, provide raw 1-minute aggregates for the disputed window.
6) Follow-up: Product/Eng propose any control changes (autoscale policy tweaks, queue sizing) and track implementation in a follow-up Linear ticket.
autoscale_policy_interaction: Autoscale policies are treated as first-class controls in the commitment. Contracted pools will have a primary autoscale policy (min, target, max GPUs), burst allowance (seconds per day), and a preemption class list. Credits are only measured after accounting for configured autoscale actions: if autoscale did not trigger due to configuration, the shortfall is attributable to customer configuration rather than Redwood service and will be excluded from credit calculations unless Redwood's autoscale engine failed to launch available capacity within the autoscale SLA window.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Spec document reviewed and signed off by SRE, Legal, and Sales.
A2: Measurement queries (PromQL/SQL) and dashboards implemented and validated on test customers in staging.
A3: Sample contract amendment language reviewed by Legal and included in new Dedicated quotes.
A4: Playbook steps validated in a simulated degraded-capacity test run and time to credit computed end-to-end.
comments: 2025-01-29 — Liam O.: Initial engineering feasibility review — measuring tokens/sec per customer at 1-min resolution is cheap; concern about p99 tail data retention costs. Suggest downsampled retention for older windows.
2025-02-02 — Legal (Maya R.): We prefer explicit exclusion text for customer-side misconfiguration and a 30-day dispute window; also recommend adding language around telemetry export formats.
2025-02-06 — SRE (Diego H.): Proposed autoscale SLA window = 10 minutes from scale signal to capacity readiness for warm GPU types; add a metric to track scale-latency per AZ.
2025-02-10 — Sales (Priya S.): Need short contract blurb that can go into quotes and a one-paragraph explanation for account teams to explain proportional credits to customers.
2025-02-14 — PM (Aisha P.): Updated measurement windows and added playbook step to include spill-to-hosted fallback where customer opt-in exists. Preparing draft for Legal signoff next week.
